details:
In desktop third person view, allow clicking a point on the ground to move there. This is the standard movement scheme in Second Life and IMVU. It would be an additional option alongside WASD, not a replacement.

Why

Accessibility. Simultaneous WASD and mouse input is a real barrier for one-handed users, users with limited hand mobility, and anyone for whom sustained key input is tiring. Click-to-move requires fewer inputs and no held keys.

Touch platforms. VRChat runs on iOS and Android, where the on-screen stick is imprecise and covers part of the display with your thumb. Tap-to-move is a scheme designed for touch input in the first place.

Onboarding. Not every new user is fluent with WASD. For anyone arriving from Second Life or a similar platform, click-to-move is already familiar.

Photography and spectating. Fine-tuning where you stand while watching your own avatar in third person is a task click-to-move handles better than keyboard input.

Proposed scope

This is the part I expect to be contentious. VRChat worlds are arbitrary geometry with no navmesh, so real pathfinding isn't realistic.

A minimal version would be enough:

Move in a straight line toward the clicked point. Reuse the existing movement code, substituting the input direction.

Stop on contact with an obstacle. No re-routing, no path recalculation.

Any WASD input immediately cancels and returns to manual control.

If the target is unreachable, don't search for a path — just travel as far as possible and stop.

With this, physics, collision, and Udon trigger handling all behave exactly as they do today. No new position sync or collision edge cases.

Input conflict

Left click is already Interact/Pickup on desktop, so this can't simply be layered on top. Options:

Enable only in third person view, leaving first person unchanged

Bind to a separate input (middle click, or a modifier plus click)

Prioritize Interact when clicking an interactable, treat clicks on plain geometry as movement

Option 3 feels most natural; option 1 is by far the simplest and would be sufficient.

World author control

An option for world authors to disable it would be worth having, so that worlds built around movement restrictions — stations, no-movement zones — don't get unexpected behavior. This should fit alongside the existing movement API such as SetWalkSpeed.
title: Click-to-move for desktop users in third person view
